title: The Supreme Court Expands Presidential Power. Again.

sentences.en: Hey, I'm Benjamin Poulin and I'm Mark Ronson and welcome to The Reframers, a podcast that's all about the love of design and the culture that surrounds it.
sentences.zh: 大家好，我是本杰明·普兰，我是马克·朗森，欢迎收听《重构者》，这是一档专注于设计之美及其背后文化的播客。

sentences.en: Even back when I was DJing in nightclubs in the era of vinyl,
sentences.zh: 即使是在我那个黑胶唱片时代的夜店打碟时期，

sentences.en: every night you took 300 of your most prized possessions to work with you and you turned a DJ booth into this like living pop-up museum of beautiful 50-year-old artifacts.
sentences.zh: 你每天晚上都要带着300件最珍贵的藏品去工作，把DJ台变成了一个充满50年历史精美文物的流动快闪博物馆。

sentences.en: Listen to The Reframers from Audemars Piguet now on your favorite podcast platforMs.
sentences.zh: 现在就在你喜爱的播客平台上收听爱彼出品的《重构者》。

sentences.en: From The New York Times, I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的迈克尔·巴尔巴罗。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: In a major ruling on Monday, the Supreme Court delivered one of the biggest changes in decades to how the federal government works.
sentences.zh: 周一，最高法院作出了一项重大裁决，对联邦政府的运作方式进行了几十年来最重大的变革之一。

sentences.en: And then the court turned around and announced an exception to its own ruling.
sentences.zh: 随后，法院又转而宣布了对其自身裁决的一项例外规定。

sentences.en: Today, my colleague Anne Marimo explains what the court was up to.
sentences.zh: 今天，我的同事安妮·马里莫将为大家解读法院的意图。

sentences.en: It's Tuesday, June 30th.
sentences.zh: 今天是6月30日，星期二。

sentences.en: Anne, thank you for coming on on a busy Supreme Court day for you.
sentences.zh: 安妮，感谢你在最高法院如此忙碌的一天来到这里。

sentences.en: Appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 不客气。

sentences.en: Thanks for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢邀请。

sentences.en: So, Anne, Monday was a day of big, and I think if we're being honest, somewhat contradictory rulings, in theory, by the Supreme Court about the scope of presidential power.
sentences.zh: 安妮，周一最高法院作出了几项重大裁决，坦白说，我认为这些裁决在理论上关于总统权力的范围存在一定的矛盾。

sentences.en: So let's start with what just happened and what it means.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们从刚刚发生的事情及其含义开始说起吧。

sentences.en: So there were two big decisions on Monday.
sentences.zh: 周一共有两项重大裁决。

sentences.en: The first was a major expansion of presidential power.
sentences.zh: 第一项是关于总统权力的重大扩张。

sentences.en: It makes it far easier for presidents to fire the heads of independent agencies like the Federal Trade Commission.
sentences.zh: 它使得总统能够更容易地解雇联邦贸易委员会等独立机构的负责人。

sentences.en: It says the president can fire regulators for no reason or any reason at all.
sentences.zh: 裁决称，总统可以无理由或以任何理由解雇监管机构人员。

sentences.en: And these have been traditionally independent agencies.
sentences.zh: 而这些机构传统上一直都是独立机构。

sentences.en: So the court's decision really upends the structure of the federal government as it's been for over 100 years.
sentences.zh: 所以，法院的这一决定实际上颠覆了联邦政府一百多年来的结构。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's not every day that you hear a colleague say that 100 years of federal government precedent and practice has been upended, but that's what you just said.
sentences.zh: 听到同事说一百年的联邦政府先例和惯例被颠覆，这可不是常有的事，但你刚才确实是这么说的。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: At the heart of this case was a 90-year-old precedent from 1935 that said Congress could protect these independent regulators from being fired on a whim by the president.
sentences.zh: 此案的核心是一个1935年的90年先例，该先例规定国会可以保护这些独立监管机构免受总统的一时兴起而遭解雇。

sentences.en: And now the court said today that they can't.
sentences.zh: 而今天法院表示，他们不能再这样做了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Basically, they overruled a major precedent.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他们推翻了一个重大先例。

sentences.en: That's the first case.
sentences.zh: 这是第一个案件。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And then the second case, as you mentioned, seems somewhat contradictory.
sentences.zh: 然后是第二个案件，正如你提到的，看起来有些矛盾。

sentences.en: In this case, the court carved out an exception for the Federal Reserve, the influential central bank.
sentences.zh: 在这个案件中，法院为具有影响力的中央银行——美联储开了一个例外。

sentences.en: The court said this is a unique institution, that independence is really critical to overseeing monetary policy.
sentences.zh: 法院称这是一个独特的机构，其独立性对于监管货币政策至关重要。

sentences.en: And as you'll recall, this is the case where President Trump tried to fire Lisa Cook, one of the governors of the Federal Reserve Board.
sentences.zh: 你可能还记得，这就是特朗普总统试图解雇美联储理事会理事之一丽莎·库克的那起案件。

sentences.en: And here the court said, unlike all these other agencies, that the president can't just remove her on a whim, that there has to be cause.
sentences.zh: 在这里，法院表示，与其他所有机构不同，总统不能仅仅因为一时兴起就解雇她，必须要有正当理由。

sentences.en: And in this case, the court's decision here was a little bit technical and procedural,
sentences.zh: 在这个案件中，法院的决定有些技术性和程序性，

sentences.en: but it upholds the principle that the Federal Reserve is unique and that its independence is really critical in our system of government.
sentences.zh: 但它维护了美联储是独特的，且其独立性在我们的政府体系中至关重要的原则。

sentences.en: Got it.
sentences.zh: 明白了。

sentences.en: So in summary, the court on Monday vastly expands the president's power by saying he can pretty much fire whoever he wants from these previously, quote-unquote,
sentences.zh: 所以总结一下，法院周一极大地扩张了总统的权力，称他几乎可以随意解雇这些此前所谓的

sentences.en: independent federal agencies on a whim, without any cause, which would seem to be a major, major change to how the federal government works.
sentences.zh: 独立联邦机构的任何人，无需任何理由，这似乎是对联邦政府运作方式的一次重大、重大的改变。

sentences.en: And yet it said all of that is true except for the central bank, which is a tricky bit of legal logic that we're going to talk about.
sentences.zh: 然而，它又说除了中央银行外，上述一切皆成立，这是一种我们接下来要讨论的棘手的法律逻辑。

sentences.en: But let's start with the first case, the biggest of the two,
sentences.zh: 但让我们先从第一个案件开始，这是两案中影响最大的一个，

sentences.en: that gives the president this power to fire so many leaders of federal agencies that previously he couldn't and overturns these decades and decades of precedent.
sentences.zh: 它赋予了总统解雇许多此前无法解雇的联邦机构领导人的权力，并推翻了数十年的先例。

sentences.en: So the first case is about Rebecca Slaughter, a Democratic nominee of the Federal Trade Commission, which by design has to have both Democratic and Republican nominees.
sentences.zh: 第一个案件是关于丽贝卡·斯劳特，她是联邦贸易委员会的一名民主党提名人，该委员会按设计必须同时包含民主党和共和党的提名人。

sentences.en: She was actually appointed by President Trump in his first term,
sentences.zh: 她实际上是在特朗普总统的第一任期内被任命的，

sentences.en: and then he comes back to office again in his second term and gets rid of lots of Democratic nominees of independent agencies, including Rebecca Slaughter.
sentences.zh: 然后他在第二任期再次上台，解雇了许多独立机构的民主党提名人，包括丽贝卡·斯劳特。

sentences.en: And then she goes to court and sues.
sentences.zh: 随后她向法院提起了诉讼。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Slaughter goes to the court and says the reason President Trump is firing me, despite appointing me, is that he doesn't like my politics now.
sentences.zh: 斯劳特向法院表示，特朗普总统解雇我的原因，尽管是我任命的，是因为他现在不喜欢我的政治立场。

sentences.en: And that's not legally sufficient, given all these legal protections that surround the kind of commission I'm on.
sentences.zh: 考虑到我所在委员会享有的所有法律保护，这在法律上是不充分的。

sentences.en: And just remind us why these particular agencies have these specific job protections.
sentences.zh: 请提醒我们为什么这些特定机构拥有这些具体的职位保护。

sentences.en: Yeah, there's a long history of these types of agencies that Congress intentionally created to be insulated from the whims of whoever's in the White House.
sentences.zh: 是的，这些类型的机构有着悠久的历史，国会有意创建它们，旨在使其免受白宫主人的随心所欲的影响。

sentences.en: The idea is that these agencies that are setting consumer protections and workplace protections are supposed to be free from politics and filled with technocrats and experts in these fields.
sentences.zh: 其理念是，这些制定消费者保护和工作场所保护措施的机构，应该不受政治干扰，并由这些领域的专家和技术官僚组成。

sentences.en: But despite these protections that Congress put in place,
sentences.zh: 但尽管国会实施了这些保护措施，

sentences.en: the Supreme Court's conservative majority has started chipping away at those in several decisions that really embrace this idea of the unitary executive.
sentences.zh: 最高法院的保守派多数派已经开始在几项裁决中削弱这些保护，这些裁决真正拥护了单一行政部门的理念。

sentences.en: And that is that the president is the head of the executive branch and has to be in charge of all the people who are filling these important executive branch agencies.
sentences.zh: 那就是总统是行政部门的首脑，必须负责所有在这些重要行政部门机构任职的人员。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We talked about the unitary executive theory.
sentences.zh: 我们讨论过单一行政部门理论。

sentences.en: I always have to say it several times, unitary executive theory, several times on the show with our colleague Charlie Savage.
sentences.zh: 我不得不在节目中和我们的同事查理·萨维奇多次提到它，单一行政部门理论。

sentences.en: And basically the idea is that in a well-run executive branch, no one who works for the president should be protected from accountability from that president.
sentences.zh: 基本上，这个理念是，在一个运作良好的行政部门中，任何为总统工作的人都不应免于该总统的问责。

sentences.en: And that these independent agencies like the Federal Trade Commission, like the Securities and Exchange Commission and so on,
sentences.zh: 而且这些像联邦贸易委员会、证券交易委员会等独立机构，

sentences.en: that the job protections held by the leaders of these agencies don't make any sense.
sentences.zh: 这些机构领导人所持有的职位保护毫无意义。

sentences.en: They're basically unconstitutional if you believe that the executive has true authority across his or her branch of government.
sentences.zh: 如果你认为行政首长对其政府部门拥有真正的权威，那么这些保护基本上是违宪的。

sentences.en: That's exactly right.
sentences.zh: 完全正确。

sentences.en: And John Roberts, who wrote the opinion today, has been embracing these theories since he was a young lawyer in the Reagan administration,
sentences.zh: 今天撰写意见书的约翰·罗伯茨，从他在里根政府担任年轻律师时起就一直拥护这些理论，

sentences.en: basically says that the president should not have to work with people in these executive branch agencies who don't share his views and that therefore President Trump was entitled to fire Rebecca Slaughter,
sentences.zh: 他基本上认为，总统不应该被迫与这些行政部门机构中不认同其观点的人共事，因此特朗普总统有权解雇丽贝卡·斯劳特，

sentences.en: as he did here.
sentences.zh: 正如他在这里所做的那样。

sentences.en: I mean, what the chief justice really seems to be saying is that from the moment these agencies were born,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，首席大法官真正想表达的似乎是，从这些机构诞生之日起，

sentences.en: and my recollection is that they're kind of New Deal era independent agencies, there was a flaw in their conception.
sentences.zh: 据我回忆，它们属于新政时期的独立机构，其构想就存在缺陷。

sentences.en: And that flaw was that the president couldn't fire their leaders, that their leaders would be insulated from presidential authority.
sentences.zh: 而那个缺陷就是总统无法解雇它们的领导人，它们的领导人会免受总统权威的影响。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And he's also saying that these agencies were very different than they are today.
sentences.zh: 他还表示，这些机构与今天的情况大不相同。

sentences.en: He talks about various statutes that have evolved since then that have given these agencies more executive power,
sentences.zh: 他谈到了自那时以来演变的各种法规，这些法规赋予了这些机构更多的行政权力，

sentences.en: and that's one of the reasons why the president needs to be able to control the rules that they're enforcing and the penalties that they're assessing.
sentences.zh: 这也是总统需要能够控制他们执行的规则和评估的处罚的原因之一。

sentences.en: Of course, the other side of this argument is that even if these agencies have changed, the very nature of their work, which is regulation,
sentences.zh: 当然，这种论点的另一面是，即使这些机构发生了变化，它们工作的本质，即监管，

sentences.en: the protection of consumers or investors, is unique within the executive branch and should be protected from political forces.
sentences.zh: 保护消费者或投资者，在行政部门中是独一无二的，应该受到保护，免受政治力量的影响。

sentences.en: That they require independent expertise,
sentences.zh: 它们需要独立的专业知识，

sentences.en: that whoever is deciding which publicly traded companies should be penalized by the SEC should not just be someone the president likes or agrees with,
sentences.zh: 任何决定哪些上市公司应受到证券交易委员会处罚的人，不应该只是总统喜欢或同意的人，

sentences.en: but someone who knows public financial markets inside out.
sentences.zh: 而应该是对公共金融市场了如指掌的人。

sentences.en: And also to shield them from influence from companies and various allies of the president.
sentences.zh: 同时也是为了保护他们免受公司和总统各种盟友的影响。

sentences.en: That's the idea, that they're supposed to be independent.
sentences.zh: 这就是理念，他们应该保持独立。

sentences.en: And so this is the point that the dissent makes, in today's opinion, written by Justice Sonia Sotomayor and joined by the other two liberals on the bench.
sentences.zh: 这就是索尼娅·索托马约尔大法官在今天的意见书中提出的异议点，其他两位自由派大法官也加入了该异议。

sentences.en: That the decision today, in addition to giving the president much more power, is really the court taking power for itself and deciding that these protections no longer apply,
sentences.zh: 今天的裁决除了赋予总统更多权力外，实际上是法院在为自己夺权，并裁定这些保护措施不再适用，

sentences.en: and they're saying it's going to have lasting and fundamental changes to the structure of the government.
sentences.zh: 他们表示这将对政府结构产生持久且根本性的改变。

sentences.en: Right, and our colleague who was in the courtroom for the dissent described this scene as pretty visceral.
sentences.zh: 没错，我们那位在法庭上旁听异议的同事形容当时的场景非常感人至深。

sentences.en: Yeah, so it's really unusual for the justices to read their dissents from the bench, and that's what Justice Sonia Sotomayor did today.
sentences.zh: 是的，大法官们在法庭上宣读他们的异议是非常罕见的，而这正是索尼娅·索托马约尔大法官今天所做的。

sentences.en: It's a real sign of just their deep disagreement.
sentences.zh: 这确实是他们深刻分歧的标志。

sentences.en: She went on for about five minutes, according to our colleague Ashwarya Kavi, and just looked very stoic and concerned about the implications of this decision.
sentences.zh: 据我们的同事阿什瓦里亚·卡维称，她宣读了大约五分钟，看起来非常冷静，并对这一裁决的影响感到担忧。

sentences.en: Her written dissent went on for almost 50 pages.
sentences.zh: 她书写的异议书长达近50页。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: I'll read to you what she said.
sentences.zh: 我来读读她说了什么。

sentences.en: She says, in granting the president this unbridled authority, the court upends its precedent, misconstrues our history, and sheds any pretense of judicial modesty.
sentences.zh: 她说，在赋予总统这种不受约束的权力时，法院颠覆了其先例，曲解了我们的历史，并抛弃了任何司法谦逊的伪装。

sentences.en: And for the Supreme Court, those are really strong words.
sentences.zh: 对于最高法院来说，这些话非常严厉。

sentences.en: And what do you think that Justice Sotomayor, and if we can imbue what she's saying to the other liberal justices who signed her dissent, is up to in writing that?
sentences.zh: 你认为索托马约尔大法官，如果我们可以将她的言论延伸到其他签署该异议的自由派大法官身上，在撰写这些内容时意欲何为？

sentences.en: I think the liberals, in Justice Sotomayor's dissent,
sentences.zh: 我认为自由派在索托马约尔大法官的异议中，

sentences.en: are expressing their deep frustration with a new example of the court overturning a longstanding precedent and the culmination of this longstanding goal of the conservative legal movement.
sentences.zh: 表达了他们对法院推翻长期先例这一新例子的深切沮丧，以及这是保守派法律运动长期目标的实现。

sentences.en: We've seen this time and again in recent years with the court overturning Roe v.
sentences.zh: 近年来我们一次又一次地看到这种情况，法院推翻了罗诉韦德案，

sentences.en: Wade, getting rid of affirmative action and college admissions.
sentences.zh: 废除了平权行动和大学招生政策。

sentences.en: So this is sort of a continuation of that frustration from the liberal wing of the court, which is very outnumbered with six to three.
sentences.zh: 所以这算是法院自由派阵营沮丧情绪的延续，他们在六比三的比例下处于明显的少数。

sentences.en: A final question on this first ruling.
sentences.zh: 关于第一个裁决的最后一个问题。

sentences.en: What's going to happen inside these agencies whose leaders had had these job protections and now lost them?
sentences.zh: 那些领导人曾拥有这些职位保护、现在却失去保护的机构内部会发生什么？

sentences.en: Practically speaking, what do we think it's going to look like?
sentences.zh: 从实际操作层面看，你认为会是什么样子？

sentences.en: Well, there are more than two dozen independent agencies with a similar structure.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有超过两打结构类似的独立机构。

sentences.en: And so what it means on the ground is that the president can go in and continue to try to get rid of Democratic commissioners.
sentences.zh: 所以这意味着在实际操作中，总统可以继续尝试清除民主党委员。

sentences.en: And as a result of this ruling, people won't be able to sue and cite these laws and job protections that have been on the books.
sentences.zh: 而由于这一裁决，人们将无法再援引这些法律和职位保护措施进行起诉。

sentences.en: Right after the ruling today, President Trump went on Truth Social.
sentences.zh: 在今天的裁决之后，特朗普总统立即在“真实社交”平台上发文。

sentences.en: He called this a big win.
sentences.zh: 他称这是一场大胜。

sentences.en: He said it's a historic and unprecedented ruling, one of the most important ever with respect to presidential powers.
sentences.zh: 他说这是一项历史性的、前所未有的裁决，是关于总统权力方面最重要的裁决之一。

sentences.en: Right, suggesting that he may be eager to follow up to the ruling with firings.
sentences.zh: 没错，这暗示他可能急于在裁决后进行解雇。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: But the president wasn't celebrating the court's second decision about the Federal Reserve.
sentences.zh: 但总统并没有庆祝法院关于美联储的第二个决定。

sentences.en: Because there, they made very clear that the Federal Reserve is different and is independent and the president won't have the same power over those leaders.
sentences.zh: 因为在那里，他们非常明确地表示美联储是不同的，是独立的，总统对那些领导人不会拥有同样的权力。

sentences.en: And we are going to talk about that case right after the break.
sentences.zh: 我们将在休息后讨论那个案件。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: 33 presidents.
sentences.zh: 33位总统。

sentences.en: I called the president at 430 in the morning and he answered.
sentences.zh: 我在凌晨4点30分给总统打电话，他接听了。

sentences.en: Seven decades in space.
sentences.zh: 太空中的七十年。

sentences.en: We want to see what's beyond the next star.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看下一颗恒星之外有什么。

sentences.en: A thousand consumer product guides.
sentences.zh: 一千份消费品指南。

sentences.en: Today I am testing seven mattresses.
sentences.zh: 今天我正在测试七款床垫。

sentences.en: 60 super sundaes.
sentences.zh: 60份超级圣代。

sentences.en: They were probably the best team in the league every single year.
sentences.zh: 他们几乎每年都是联盟中最好的球队。

sentences.en: 53,500 puzzles.
I use a different starting word every day.
sentences.zh: 我每天都使用不同的起始词。

sentences.en: 25,000 recipes.
And I love a one-pan recipe because I don't love washing pans.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢一锅出的食谱，因为我不喜欢洗锅。

sentences.en: The New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.en: Celebrating 175 years of helping you understand the world and make the most of each day.
sentences.zh: 庆祝175年来帮助您了解世界并充分利用每一天。

sentences.en: Subscribe now for a special offer at nytimes.com slash subscribe.
sentences.zh: 现在订阅可享受nytimes.com/subscribe的特别优惠。

sentences.en: So, Anne, let's turn now to the second Supreme Court ruling that came down on Monday revolving around the Federal Reserve.
sentences.zh: 那么，安妮，让我们转到周一作出的关于美联储的第二个最高法院裁决。

sentences.en: And how it is that the same Supreme Court got to such a different ruling when it came to the Federal Reserve than it did with all these other agencies.
sentences.zh: 为什么同一个最高法院在涉及美联储时，得出的裁决与所有其他机构如此不同？

sentences.en: Just describe that case and how the court got to the result it did.
sentences.zh: 请描述一下那个案件，以及法院是如何得出这一结果的。

sentences.en: So, this is the case of Lisa Cook, a member of the Federal Reserve Board of Governors who Trump tried to fire.
sentences.zh: 这是一个关于丽莎·库克的案件，她是特朗普试图解雇的美联储理事会成员之一。

sentences.en: You'll remember the president has been putting a lot of pressure on the Federal Reserve to lower interest rates.
sentences.zh: 你还记得总统一直向美联储施加巨大压力，要求其降低利率。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: He did not like Lisa Cook's views and policies and he fires her and he says the reason is because of these unproven allegations of mortgage fraud.
sentences.zh: 他不喜欢丽莎·库克的观点和政策，于是解雇了她，并称原因是这些未经证实的抵押贷款欺诈指控。

sentences.en: He says that she's misstated her finances on mortgage applications.
sentences.zh: 他说她在抵押贷款申请中虚报了财务状况。

sentences.en: And Lisa Cook and her lawyers soon go to court and say, you can't fire me without good cause.
sentences.zh: 丽莎·库克和她的律师很快向法院提起诉讼，称你不能在没有正当理由的情况下解雇我。

sentences.en: That's what the law says.
sentences.zh: 法律就是这么规定的。

sentences.en: And it really tees up this test for the Supreme Court.
sentences.zh: 这确实为最高法院设置了一个考验。

sentences.en: Is the Federal Reserve like these other agencies where they're questioning the job protections of regulators or is the Federal Reserve different?
sentences.zh: 美联储是否像其他机构一样，正在质疑监管机构的职位保护，还是美联储有所不同？

sentences.en: Because the lawsuit involving the Federal Trade Commission and Trump's decision to fire one of the leaders there and this case involving Lisa Cook and his decision to fire her from the Federal Reserve,
sentences.zh: 因为涉及联邦贸易委员会的诉讼和特朗普解雇其中一名领导人的决定，以及这个涉及丽莎·库克和特朗普决定将她从美联储解雇的案件，

sentences.en: they're happening more or less simultaneously in the court system and they're very much speaking to each other.
sentences.zh: 它们在法院系统中几乎是同时发生的，而且它们在很大程度上是相互呼应的。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And here we see in Lisa Cook's case, the court says very clearly the Federal Reserve is different and has a unique history that Lisa Cook can only be fired for cause.
sentences.zh: 在这里，我们看到在丽莎·库克的案件中，法院非常明确地表示美联储是不同的，拥有独特的历史，丽莎·库克只能因正当理由被解雇。

sentences.en: And they lay out all sorts of reasons why she needs to have a different process here if Trump wants to fire her.
sentences.zh: 他们列举了各种原因，说明如果特朗普想解雇她，为什么她需要一个不同的程序。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: The Supreme Court is not saying that someday Trump can't fire Lisa Cook.
sentences.zh: 最高法院并不是说特朗普将来不能解雇丽莎·库克。

sentences.en: The court is saying that the way he fired her was wrong based on the unique job protections afforded to the Federal Reserve.
sentences.zh: 法院是说他解雇她的方式是错误的，因为美联储享有独特的职位保护。

sentences.en: But help me understand why the court distinguishes the Federal Reserve and the need to have cause to fire someone like Lisa Cook from all these other agencies we talked about in the first half of our conversation where apparently you don't need cause.
sentences.zh: 但请帮我理解，为什么法院将美联储以及解雇像丽莎·库克这样的人需要正当理由的必要性，与我们在前半部分谈到的所有其他机构区分开来，在那些机构中显然不需要正当理由。

sentences.en: So both of the opinions on Monday were written by Chief Justice John Roberts, but the Federal Reserve case had a very different lineup.
sentences.zh: 周一的两项裁决均由首席大法官约翰·罗伯茨撰写，但联邦储备委员会案的法官阵容却大不相同。

sentences.en: You had all three liberal justices and Trump nominee Brett Kavanaugh joining the Chief Justice to carve out this exception for the Federal Reserve.
sentences.zh: 三位自由派大法官和特朗普提名的布雷特·卡瓦诺加入了首席大法官的行列，为联邦储备委员会开辟了这一例外情况。

sentences.en: And they spend a lot of time explaining why there's this exception.
sentences.zh: 他们花费了大量篇幅来解释为何存在这一例外。

sentences.en: They talk about the history of the Federal Reserve.
sentences.zh: 他们谈到了联邦储备委员会的历史。

sentences.en: They keep talking about its unique role in our economy and in the world economy and talking about how crucial its independence is.
sentences.zh: 他们不断谈论其在我国经济乃至世界经济中的独特作用，并强调其独立性是多么至关重要。

sentences.en: And that's why they say it's different.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们说它与众不同的原因。

sentences.en: I just want to dwell on this for a minute because I'm sure to some people it will make total sense.
sentences.zh: 我想就这一点多说几句，因为我相信对某些人来说，这完全说得通。

sentences.en: But I'm sure to others it seems like a very strange distinction to say that the president can have free reign in every agency in the executive branch even when it was supposed to be independent as envisioned by Congress except for this one.
sentences.zh: 但我也肯定，对另一些人来说，这似乎是一个非常奇怪的区分——即总统可以在行政部门的每个机构中拥有绝对权力，即使是国会设想中本应独立的机构，除了这一个之外。

sentences.en: Because is the safety of a child protected by, you know, the Consumer Product Safety Commission or the companies that are regulated by the Securities and Exchange Commission?
sentences.zh: 因为，孩子的安全是由消费品安全委员会保护的，还是由证券交易委员会监管的公司保护的？

sentences.en: Are they that much less important than the work done by the Federal Reserve?
sentences.zh: 它们真的比联邦储备委员会所做的工作重要性低那么多吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, I think it was significant that the court heard in amicus briefs from former top Treasury officials and former Fed chairman.
sentences.zh: 是的，我认为法院听取了前财政部高官和前美联储主席提交的法庭之友陈述，这一点意义重大。

sentences.en: They warned the court that if they allowed the president to remove Lisa Cook while this litigation was underway, there would be widespread consequences for the global economy,
sentences.zh: 他们警告法院，如果允许总统在诉讼期间罢免丽莎·库克，将对全球经济产生广泛影响，

sentences.en: for interest rates, and that it was really critical to protect the autonomy of the nation's central bank in an outsized way from these other agencies.
sentences.zh: 对利率也会产生影响，而且在很大程度上保护国家央行免受这些其他机构的影响至关重要。

sentences.en: I wonder if these former Treasury secretaries are making a legal distinction, what makes the Fed different from these other agencies,
sentences.zh: 我不知道这些前财政部长们是在进行法律上的区分，即是什么让美联储区别于其他机构，

sentences.en: or are they making a kind of a practical policy distinction?
sentences.zh: 还是他们是在进行一种实际政策上的区分？

sentences.en: And if the majority adopted their views, which they have, are they embracing a legal distinction here or just a practical policy distinction?
sentences.zh: 如果多数派采纳了他们的观点（他们确实采纳了），那么他们在这里采用的是法律上的区分，还是仅仅是实际政策上的区分？

sentences.en: That's a good question.
sentences.zh: 这是一个好问题。

sentences.en: In dissent, Justice Clarence Thomas says that these are policy arguments for an independent bank,
sentences.zh: 克拉伦斯·托马斯大法官在异议中表示，这些是支持独立银行的政策论点，

sentences.en: but that actually it's not constitutional if the president doesn't have free reign to fire independent regulators.
sentences.zh: 但如果总统没有解雇独立监管机构负责人的绝对权力，这实际上是不符合宪法的。

sentences.en: Basically, Thomas is saying that you cannot grant the president the freedom to fire everybody and all these other agencies and carve out the exception of the Fed.
sentences.zh: 基本上，托马斯是在说，你不能授予总统解雇所有其他机构所有人的自由，却又为美联储开辟例外。

sentences.en: What's good for the goose should be good for the gander, and you guys have screwed this up.
sentences.zh: 己所不欲，勿施于人，你们把这事搞砸了。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: So, Anne, what happens now to Lisa Cook?
sentences.zh: 那么，安，丽莎·库克现在会怎样？

sentences.en: She seems like she's still in a pretty severe state of legal limbo.
sentences.zh: 她似乎仍处于一种相当严重的法律困境中。

sentences.en: Yeah, this was a narrow victory for her today.
sentences.zh: 是的，这对她来说今天是一场微弱的胜利。

sentences.en: The court is not saying that Trump can never fire her.
sentences.zh: 法院并没有说特朗普永远不能解雇她。

sentences.en: It's just saying that the way he did it was improper and that she deserves some sort of process.
sentences.zh: 只是说他解雇的方式是不当的，她理应得到某种正当程序。

sentences.en: And for a court that gets criticized for not checking the president, here they're calling these allegations half-hearted.
sentences.zh: 对于一个因未能制衡总统而受到批评的法院来说，他们在这里称这些指控为敷衍了事。

sentences.en: They're saying that trying to fire someone in a social media post was not the right process.
sentences.zh: 他们是说，试图通过社交媒体帖子解雇某人并不是正确的程序。

sentences.en: And they're basically saying, if you want to do this, you need to try again and to do it the proper way.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上是在说，如果你想这样做，你需要重来，并以正确的方式进行。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's striking to me that you bring up the subject of this court and Trump's power because that's where I'd like to end our conversation, Anne.
sentences.zh: 你提到了这个法院和特朗普权力的话题，这让我很惊讶，因为我想以此结束我们的谈话，安。

sentences.en: So, let's talk about how these two cases fit into our larger understanding of this entire term when it comes to presidential power.
sentences.zh: 那么，让我们谈谈这两个案件如何融入我们对本届最高法院在总统权力方面的整体理解。

sentences.en: I know the term isn't over.
sentences.zh: 我知道本届任期还没结束。

sentences.en: However, there's at least one major ruling still in the offing, which is birthright citizenship.
sentences.zh: 然而，至少还有一个重大裁决即将出炉，那就是出生公民权问题。

sentences.en: The president has tried to end it by executive order.
sentences.zh: 总统曾试图通过行政命令终止它。

sentences.en: We think, based on reporting that you and our colleagues have done and based on the questions that the justices have asked in oral arguments,
sentences.zh: 根据你和我们同事所做的报道，以及大法官们在口头辩论中提出的问题，我们认为，

sentences.en: that they are likely to find against the president when it comes to birthright citizenship.
sentences.zh: 在出生公民权问题上，他们很可能会做出不利于总统的裁决。

sentences.en: So, if we speculate for just a moment that that is how that case ends and we look at the entire term,
sentences.zh: 所以，如果我们暂时推测这就是该案的结局，并审视整个任期，

sentences.en: how should we think about where this court, in the beginning of Trump's second term, has landed on the question of presidential power?
sentences.zh: 我们应该如何看待这个法院在特朗普第二个任期开始时，在总统权力问题上的立场？

sentences.en: I think, depending on what happens on the final day, what we've seen is the court's conservative majority picking some key issues to stand up to President Trump on,
sentences.zh: 我认为，取决于最后一天发生什么，我们所看到的是法院的保守派多数派挑选了一些关键议题来对抗特朗普总统，

sentences.en: especially issues that were personally important to him.
sentences.zh: 尤其是那些对他个人而言很重要的议题。

sentences.en: As you'll remember, some of the conservative justices joined with the liberals to strike down his sweeping tariffs.
sentences.zh: 正如你所记得的，一些保守派大法官与自由派联手否决了他的全面关税政策。

sentences.en: And if we do see them push back on birthright citizenship, that's something that's very important to him.
sentences.zh: 如果我们确实看到他们对出生公民权进行回击，那对他来说是非常重要的事情。

sentences.en: As you'll recall, the president showed up in the courtroom, the first sitting president to do so, to watch that.
sentences.zh: 正如你所记得的，总统出现在法庭上，成为第一位这样做的在任总统，以观看庭审。

sentences.en: But the overall takeaway is that it's a term where the court has really expanded presidential power,
sentences.zh: 但总的结论是，这是一个法院真正扩大了总统权力的任期，

sentences.en: in particular on immigration and on a president's ability to fire government officials.
sentences.zh: 特别是在移民问题和总统解雇政府官员的能力方面。

sentences.en: We saw this last week with the removal of protections for Haitians and Syrians who have been living and working in this country legally.
sentences.zh: 我们上周看到了这一点，当时取消了对在该国合法居住和工作的海地人和叙利亚人的保护。

sentences.en: And then we're seeing today the power to fire traditionally independent regulators.
sentences.zh: 然后我们今天看到了解雇传统上独立监管机构负责人的权力。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And on the other side of presidential power, of course, is frequently Congress.
sentences.zh: 而在总统权力的另一面，当然通常是国会。

sentences.en: And in the bigger of the two rulings on Monday, as you said, Anne, power was taken from Congress.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说的，安，在周一两项裁决中较大的一项中，权力从国会手中被夺走了。

sentences.en: Because these four cause job protections, this idea that you can't just fire somebody on a whim, that was created by Congress and the court just overturned it.
sentences.zh: 因为这四个导致就业保护的原因，即你不能仅仅因为一时兴起就解雇某人的想法，这是由国会创造的，而法院刚刚推翻了它。

sentences.en: Similarly, this court has weakened the Voting Rights Act, a major achievement of Congress.
sentences.zh: 同样，这个法院削弱了《投票权法案》，这是国会的一项重大成就。

sentences.en: States can now break up black majority districts under a ruling by this court from not so long ago.
sentences.zh: 根据这个法院不久前的一项裁决，各州现在可以拆分黑人占多数的选区。

sentences.en: And if you step back even further, in the many years I have been thinking about this court,
sentences.zh: 如果你退后一步，在我思考这个法院的许多年里，

sentences.en: it has been undoing the work of Congress, I think, about Citizens United and how that gutted campaign finance reform.
sentences.zh: 我认为它一直在撤销国会的工作，比如关于《公民联合》案以及它如何掏空了竞选财务改革。

sentences.en: I mean, when we think about this court and presidential power, should we be thinking not just about president and power,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，当我们思考这个法院和总统权力时，我们是否应该思考的不仅仅是总统和权力，

sentences.en: but about this conservative majority on this court pretty systematically weakening Congress?
sentences.zh: 而是这个法院的保守派多数派在相当系统地削弱国会？

sentences.en: Or should we think of it as putting Congress in its place?
sentences.zh: 还是我们应该认为这是在让国会各安其位？

sentences.en: Yeah, it's all about the balance of power.
sentences.zh: 是的，这完全是关于权力平衡的问题。

sentences.en: And as you say, they are expanding the president's power.
sentences.zh: 正如你所说，他们正在扩大总统的权力。

sentences.en: They are restraining Congress's power.
sentences.zh: 他们正在限制国会的权力。

sentences.en: And at the same time, the conservative majority is taking power for the court.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，保守派多数派正在为法院夺取权力。

sentences.en: That they get to say, you know, whether or not the Voting Rights Act is still needed in this way.
sentences.zh: 他们有权决定，你知道，是否还需要以这种方式保留《投票权法案》。

sentences.en: And similarly, you know, whether they're saying Congress can't constrain the president
sentences.zh: 同样，你知道，他们是否在说国会不能限制总统

sentences.en: when it comes to firing independent agency officials, despite laws they passed many years ago.
sentences.zh: 在解雇独立机构官员方面，尽管国会多年前通过了相关法律。

sentences.en: So by weakening Congress, the court is to some degree not just strengthening the executive, it's strengthening the judiciary.
sentences.zh: 因此，通过削弱国会，法院在某种程度上不仅是在加强行政部门，它还在加强司法部门。

sentences.en: It's strengthening itself.
sentences.zh: 它在加强自身。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: I never thought of it that way.
sentences.zh: 我从来没有那样想过。

sentences.en: I just want to end by meditating for just a moment on the work that a conservative legal movement has accomplished.
sentences.zh: 我想最后沉思片刻，谈谈保守派法律运动所取得的成就。

sentences.en: Because this ruling does feel like a capstone to that movement.
sentences.zh: 因为这项裁决确实感觉像是该运动的基石。

sentences.en: And it's built on this idea that the presidency should be more powerful.
sentences.zh: 它建立在总统权力应该更强大的理念之上。

sentences.en: Yes, power gets distributed around.
sentences.zh: 是的，权力得到了分配。

sentences.en: Maybe the court's getting a little more powerful.
sentences.zh: 也许法院变得更强大了一些。

sentences.en: But at the end of the day, it's the presidency that's gotten the most powerful because of these court rulings over the past many years.
sentences.zh: 但归根结底，由于过去多年来的这些法院裁决，总统职位变得最强大了。

sentences.en: And because it's a conservative legal movement, it feels like one that has been accomplished in the pursuit of conservative goals.
sentences.zh: 而且因为它是一场保守派法律运动，感觉它是在追求保守派目标的过程中完成的。

sentences.en: But the power that's been given to the president will outlive this president by a long time and perhaps, right,
sentences.zh: 但赋予总统的权力将比这位总统长久得多，也许，对吧，

sentences.en: end up in the hands of a Democratic president who will use it for entirely different ends.
sentences.zh: 最终会落入一位民主党总统手中，他将把这些权力用于完全不同的目的。

sentences.en: That's right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: We tend to think about these decisions in terms of President Trump and what can he do in the moment.
sentences.zh: 我们倾向于从特朗普总统的角度以及他当下能做什么来考虑这些决定。

sentences.en: But these rulings will outlast him and this power will apply to whoever is in the White House and will be very long lasting.
sentences.zh: 但这些裁决将比他更长久，这种权力将适用于白宫的任何人，并将产生非常持久的影响。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And could, in theory, lead to, instead of deregulation, some of the most far-reaching regulations we've had in decades?
sentences.zh: 从理论上讲，这是否会导致一些几十年来最深远的监管，而不是放松监管？

sentences.en: We don't know because we've only really experienced it in recent history through the prism of a maximalist Republican president.
sentences.zh: 我们不知道，因为我们在近代史上真正体验到的只是通过一位极权主义共和党总统的视角。

sentences.en: Well, I've talked to lots of legal analysts on the left who say this decision, yes, it will upend the structure of the government.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我和许多左翼法律分析人士谈过，他们说这个决定，是的，它将颠覆政府的结构。

sentences.en: But it means that if a Democrat comes into the White House next,
sentences.zh: 但这意味着如果下一任是民主党人入主白宫，

sentences.en: that person will have a lot more freedom to get rid of those commissioners and fire those commissioners that Trump has appointed and to change the direction of these agencies.
sentences.zh: 那个人将有更多的自由去摆脱那些委员，解雇特朗普任命的那些委员，并改变这些机构的方向。

sentences.en: So as much as President Trump has remade this government in his image, these rulings, which, because he created this conservative majority in a way he's partly responsible for,
sentences.zh: 所以，尽管特朗普总统以他的形象重塑了这个政府，但这些裁决——因为他创造了这个保守派多数派，他在某种程度上负有部分责任——

sentences.en: will help cede the next Democratic president undoing this.
sentences.zh: 将有助于为下一任民主党总统撤销这一切埋下伏笔。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 正是如此。

sentences.en: Because of this ruling, whenever the pendulum swings in the other direction, it's going to swing hard.
sentences.zh: 因为这项裁决，无论何时钟摆向另一个方向摆动，它都会摆动得很剧烈。

sentences.en: And ironically, that's what the dissent said in Monday's first ruling, that these agencies were intentionally structured to be bipartisan, to be filled with experts,
sentences.zh: 讽刺的是，这正是周一第一项裁决中异议所说的，这些机构被有意设计为两党制，由专家组成，

sentences.en: and to not change depending on who was in the White House.
sentences.zh: 并且不会根据谁入主白宫而改变。

sentences.en: But because of the court's ruling on Monday, that's exactly what's going to happen.
sentences.zh: 但由于法院周一的裁决，这正是将会发生的事情。

sentences.en: Anne, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 安，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: We appreciate it.
sentences.zh: 我们很感激。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: I'm Winnalou.
sentences.zh: 我是温娜露。

sentences.en: I write the game Connections, one of the puzzles from New York Times Games, and I love horror movies.
sentences.zh: 我编写《Connections》游戏，这是《纽约时报》游戏中的谜题之一，我喜欢恐怖电影。

sentences.en: I love my dog, and I love trying to trick you.
sentences.zh: 我爱我的狗，我也喜欢尝试戏弄你。

sentences.en: I'm Sam Mazursky, and I create the game Spelling Bee and Letterboxd on a daily basis.
sentences.zh: 我是萨姆·马祖斯基，我每天创作《Spelling Bee》和《Letterboxd》游戏。

sentences.en: And I have this thing called Chromesthesia.
sentences.zh: 我有一种叫做“联觉”的东西。

sentences.en: I see color when I'm listening to music.
sentences.zh: 我在听音乐时能看到颜色。

sentences.en: New York Times games are made by people, like the ones you just heard from.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》的游戏是由像你刚才听到的人那样的人制作的。

sentences.en: Go to nytimes.com slash games to start playing today.
sentences.zh: 前往 nytimes.com/games 今天就开始玩吧。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要知道的其他消息。

sentences.en: The Supreme Court issued two other notable rulings on Monday.
sentences.zh: 最高法院周一还发布了另外两项值得注意的裁决。

sentences.en: In one of them, the court upheld state laws, allowing ballots to be counted even if they arrive by mail after Election Day.
sentences.zh: 其中一项裁决中，法院支持了各州的法律，允许即使在选举日之后通过邮件送达的选票也被计入。

sentences.en: Democrats vote by mail in larger numbers than Republicans,
sentences.zh: 民主党人通过邮件投票的人数比共和党人多，

sentences.en: and the ruling was a blow to President Trump's attempt to restrict voting in ways that he hopes will advantage Republicans in the midterm elections.
sentences.zh: 这项裁决对特朗普总统试图以他希望在期中选举中对共和党有利的方式限制投票的企图是一个打击。

sentences.en: Meanwhile, the Supreme Court declined Trump's request to review a $5 million civil judgment against him.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，最高法院拒绝了特朗普要求复审针对他的一项500万美元民事判决的请求。

sentences.en: The judgment stemmed from a 2023 trial in which a jury in Manhattan found Trump liable for sexually assaulting and defaming the journalist E.
sentences.zh: 该判决源于2023年的一场审判，曼哈顿的一个陪审团认定特朗普对性侵犯和诽谤记者E·

sentences.en: Jean Carroll.
sentences.zh: 珍·卡罗尔负有责任。

sentences.en: Trump has repeatedly denied the accusations.
sentences.zh: 特朗普一再否认这些指控。

sentences.zh: 今天的节目由克莱尔·坦内斯凯特和莱克西·迪奥制作，尼娜·费尔德曼提供了帮助。

sentences.en: It was edited by Devin Taylor and Patricia Willans, and contains music by Marian Lozano.
sentences.zh: 节目由德文·泰勒和帕特里夏·威兰斯编辑，包含玛丽安·洛萨诺的音乐。

sentences.en: Our theme music is by Wonderly.
sentences.zh: 我们的主题音乐由Wonderly创作。

sentences.en: This episode was engineered by Chris Wood.
sentences.zh: 本期节目由克里斯·伍德进行工程制作。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 这就是《The Daily》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: This week on The Wirecutter Show, we're getting ready for hosting over the holidays.
sentences.zh: 本周在《Wirecutter Show》节目中，我们正在为假期接待客人做准备。

sentences.en: Tune in for tips on making your guests feel at home.
sentences.zh: 收听节目，获取让客人感到宾至如归的秘诀。

sentences.en: Are they a blackout sleeper?
sentences.zh: 他们是需要完全遮光才能入睡的人吗？

sentences.en: I don't mean do they blackout to go to sleep.
sentences.zh: 我不是指他们是否昏睡过去才入睡。

sentences.en: I mean, what kind of light do they require?
sentences.zh: 我是指，他们需要什么样的光线？

sentences.en: Because that is a very specific thing.
sentences.zh: 因为那是一件非常具体的事情。

sentences.en: Do they have allergies, food sensitivities?
sentences.zh: 他们有过敏症或食物敏感吗？

sentences.en: Are they coffee tea drinkers?
sentences.zh: 他们是喝咖啡还是喝茶的人？

sentences.en: What time do they like to get up?
sentences.zh: 他们喜欢几点起床？

sentences.en: Find The Wirecutter Show on the New York Times app or wherever you like to listen.
sentences.zh: 在《纽约时报》应用程序或你喜欢的任何地方找到《Wirecutter Show》。
